LSE 0.5.3 loads models several times faster, decodes faster, makes CPU fallback refusable everywhere it can happen and builds the iOS framework against the current mac_linuxgpu HSA runtime. The fallback behavior is specified in [docs/API.md](https://github.com/Geramy/LSE/blob/v0.5.3/docs/API.md#cpu-fallback).

**Requires mac_linuxgpu v0.1.151 (build 255) or later** on macOS. The measurements below were taken on build 255.

## Changes

1. **`--no-cpu-fallback` on `lse` and `lse-server`.** With it, startup fails when no device backend comes up or `--pool` names a CPU device, and a request fails when an operation has no device kernel. Each error names the cause. Without it, CPU fallback still runs, and it is logged, counted in `lse_status` and reported in `lse_warnings`.
2. **No CPU-only run with the option.** Before this release, without `--pool`, a GPU backend that failed to start left the whole model on the CPU interpreter with a warning, even with `--no-cpu-fallback`. The option now refuses that case, the same way `--pool hrx:0` does. `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1` has the same effect as the option.
3. **iOS build against mac_linuxgpu build 247 and later** (tested on 246 and 247). `scripts/ios/build-ios.sh` builds with the runtime's owner and selector calls (async session calls). It builds the HSA runtime under `build/ios/hsa`, so the mac_linuxgpu checkout is only read. With `SKIP_HRX=1`, it now links the HSA runtime it just built, not the one an earlier run used. The script is executable. The published framework is built against build 255.
4. **Faster model load.** The pinned Qwen3.8-27B Q4 + DFlash2 configuration loads in **3.9 s** on driver build 255 with a 16 GT/s link, down from 16–28 s. Weight uploads stream through a ring of mapped staging buffers, so reading the checkpoint (with `pread`) overlaps the copy to the GPU instead of alternating with it. RoPE tables are computed on all cores and uploaded once, the server loads the tokenizer while the weights upload, and load-time host buffers are mapped and unmapped so the loaded server does not keep them resident. `LSE_TIME_LOAD=1` prints the time of each load phase.
5. **Faster decode.** A 640-token decode is about **4%** faster. Speculative verify logits are read a row at a time as the acceptance walk needs them, and the small per-step host writes (token ids, DFlash2 draft inputs, the prefix-commit descriptor) are queued behind the stream instead of waiting for the GPU to go idle.

## Performance

Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with the Q8 DFlash2 draft on an R9700, mac_linuxgpu build 255 (16 GT/s link), `--batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --kv-cache-dtype bf16`:

| Prompt | Prefill (tok/s) | Decode (tok/s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2K | 592 | 28.5 |
| 4K | 628 | 38.4 |

Model load: 3.9 s (16–28 s in 0.5.2).

## Downloads

| Asset | For |
| --- | --- |
| `lse-v0.5.3-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon with an external AMD GPU and the [mac_linuxgpu](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/mac_linuxgpu) driver |
| `lse-v0.5.3-ios-arm64.xcframework.zip` | iOS/iPadOS 26+ apps that embed the mac_linuxgpu driver; contains `LSE.xcframework` |
| `lse-v0.5.3-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux x86_64 with ROCm 7.x |

Each asset has a `.sha256` beside it. The C ABI version is unchanged (`LSE_ABI_VERSION` 1). `lse_config.disable_cpu_fallback` keeps its place and now also covers startup.
